selection.rule: Actual parts: lowest VA, then smallest reservoir, with zero flagged cases over the full matrix. Inquiry specification: corner-screened sweep, stock primary preferred, then lowest VA, smallest reservoir and widest margin; the pick is confirmed on the full matrix. A screen result for supplier inquiry and bench proof. No purchase or native adoption.

inquiry_sweep.corners: Per mode: 0.9 mains with expansion_stress, full budget and minus-tolerance reservoir; 1.1 mains idle baseline and 1.1 mains expansion_stress full budget at both reservoir tolerances.
inquiry_sweep.basis: Triad 50 VA and 100 VA typical regulation reused at another loaded voltage. dedicated_120_220 means primaries wound for 120 V and 220 V so the ratio error of a 115/230 V part is absent. Not existing part numbers.

limitations: Transformer model is a resistive equivalent from typical regulation at 25 C. No measured winding resistance, secondary voltage tolerance, leakage, core flux or temperature rise.
Operating a 115/230 V primary at 132 V or 242 V is an engineering screen, not a manufacturer approval.
Regulators are imposed loads. No dropout, startup, protection or stability model. Heat uses the contract minimum-output corners and an assumed 6 C/W junction-to-sink path.
Guarded-mute and optical currents are the stated budgets applied continuously to every profile; the baseline budget bounds the unloaded raw maximum.
Reservoir ESR is the contract 0.15 ohm for both sizes. Ripple-current rating, lifetime and fit are not checked.
Worst-phase surge is a closed-form bound against the surrogate resistance only; the rectifier surge rating was not verified here.
Inquiry options are hypothetical windings. Their regulation, size and availability are unknown until a supplier answers.
No chassis fit, fuse, heatsink, supplier stock or delivery evidence.
